division.heading: Lawyers’ Charges, Retainer Agreements and Right of Review

operative_text.controlling:
10.13(1)  A lawyer or a client may, by request, obtain from a
review officer an appointment date for a review of a retainer
agreement or a lawyer’s charges, or both.
(2)  If a lawyer obtains an appointment date, the lawyer must file
(a) a notice of the appointment in Form 42,
(b) a copy of any retainer agreement between the lawyer and
the client, and
(c) if the appointment is for a review of the lawyer’s charges,
a copy of a signed account of the lawyer’s charges that are
to be reviewed.
(3)  If a client obtains an appointment date, the client must file
(a) a notice of the appointment in Form 42,
(b) a copy of any retainer agreement between the lawyer and
the client, if a copy is available, and
(c) if the appointment is for a review of a lawyer’s charges, a
copy of the lawyer’s account that is to be reviewed, if a
copy is available.
(4)  The client or the lawyer who obtains an appointment date for
review must serve copies of the documents filed under subrule (2)
or (3) on the other party to the review and any other interested
party 10 days or more before the appointment date, or within any
other period specified by a review officer.
(5)  A notice of appointment must be filed, endorsed and served in
the same manner as a commencement document.

BOOK_A.title: Appointment for Review
BOOK_A.commentary:
The Court of King's Bench website under the link “Reviews & Assessments” has a link to
an online request form to book a review hearing, contact information to the relevant ofﬁces in
Calgary and Edmonton, and a list with links to 10 court notices from August 2020 to January
2022. Most are general topics, but some still very relevant. During the Covid epidemic, reviews
and assessments were all by telephone, but presumably that is no longer so.
Subrule (5) is new in 2020.
Where some objections to the account are within the jurisdiction of a review ofﬁcer and some
not, see the Twinn case.¹
On the interactions of the time limits involved, see the Rath case,²
and see R.10.10 itself.
On what is a sufﬁcient signature, cf. the Elliott case.³
The court criticized a client who asked to have the account taxed, and then (on taxation)
objected to the jurisdiction of the taxing ofﬁcer.⁴
The usual lax tests for amending pleadings apply to amending such an appointment.⁵
On ﬁling a bill of costs and back-up, see R.10.14n.

footnotes.text: Twinn v. Sawridge, supra, R.10.10n. And see R.10.17n and 10.18n.
R. v. Elliott 2013 ABCA 249, Calg 1101 0068A (one JA Jul 10).
Shreem Hldg. v. Barr Picard (#1) 2013 ABQB 257, 560 AR 272.
Borden Ladner & Co. v. CBI Invs.2016 ABQB 220, 89 CPC(7th) 399.

BOOK_B.title: Appointment for review

commentary.text: Rule 10.13 See Alberta Rules of Court, Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 10.13. Lawyers on Legal Aid In P., Barristers & Solicitors v. Legal Aid Society (Alberta) (1994), 26 Alta. L.R. (3d) 167 (Q.B.), Madam Justice Fruman concluded that lawyers who act for clients through Legal Aid have contractually opted out of the taxation provisions of the Rules. Therefore, those lawyers are not persons “entitled to tax any costs” under R. 630. At p. 176 of her decision she said: By signing the certificate the Applicants contractually agreed to follow the procedures set out in the Legal Aid Rules, including the finality of the decision of the Exceptional Accounts Review Committee. Rule 630 provides that “a person entitled to tax any costs” shall secure an appointment for taxation from the taxing officer. It follows from my analysis that the Applicants are not entitled to tax their costs in light of their contract as evidenced by the certificates.

BOOK_C.title: Appointment for review

commentary.text:
Rules 10.9 and 10.13(1) bestow on a client the right to ask a review officer to assess the reasonableness of a retainer agreement. Steinke v. Hajduk Gibbs LLP, [2014] A.J. No. 62, 2014 ABQB 34 at footnote 10 (Alta. Q.B.). A court must hold the lawyer and the client to promises made in a retainer agreement. Steinke v. Hajduk Gibbs LLP, [2014] A.J. No. 62, 2014 ABQB 34 at para. 51 (Alta. Q.B.).
A “client” includes “a person who is or may be liable to pay or who has paid lawyer’s charges or part of them”. Fleming v. Fleming Alberta , [2020] A.J. No. 142, 2020 ABQB 85 at paras. 26-30 (Alta. Q.B.); Treasury Branches v. 1401057 Alberta Ltd (c.o.b. Katch 22) . , [2013] A.J. No. 1449, 2013 ABQB 748 at footnote 3 (Alta. Q.B.); and definitions (contained in an appendix to those rules). Alberta Rules of Court

commentary.review_flag: (1) The commentary ('General Principles', 809 characters) is cut off after the words 'Alberta Rules of Court' (no closing sentence). 'Rules 10.9 and 10.13(1) bestow on a client the right to ask a review officer to assess the reasonableness of a retainer agreement. Steinke v. Hajduk Gibbs LLP, [2014] A.J. No. 62, 2014 ABQB 34 at footnote 10': agrees with the rules (official 10.13(1) lets a client obtain an appointment for a review of a retainer agreement; 10.9 makes retainer agreements reviewable) and with Book B's 10.9 commentary (Steinke para 51 carries footnote marker '10' after 'retainer agreement'; the text of that footnote is not printed in Book B, and neither Book A nor Book B cites '10.13(1)' for it). 'A court must hold the lawyer and the client to promises made in a retainer agreement. Steinke ... at para. 51' agrees with Book B (para 51: 'The third principle is that a court must hold the lawyer and the client to promises made in a retainer agreement ... in the absence of a compelling reason not to'). 'A "client" includes "a person who is or may be liable to pay or who has paid lawyer's charges or part of them"' agrees with the Appendix definition (official line 40619); the Fleming (paras 26-30), Katch 22 and 'definitions (contained in an appendix to those rules)' citations are the same as in the 10.11 commentary and are not tied to the appointment procedure of 10.13. Nothing in the passage is about the filing and service steps of subrules (2)-(5), and Book B's commentary (Legal Aid lawyers and old R. 630) is not in Book C. The passage is kept as printed (flagged).
